result:
I wrote `src/test/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtilsAgentTest.java` (50 test methods, JUnit 3 `TestCase` style matching the rest of the package). 48 tests pass; 2 fail, and both failures reveal real bugs in `NumberUtils`, not test bugs:

1. **`testCreateNumberTrailingDot`** — `NumberUtils.createNumber("1.")` throws `NumberFormatException` instead of returning `1.0`. A trailing decimal point with no digits after it (e.g. `"1."`) is a valid Java floating-point literal (`Double.valueOf("1.")` == `1.0`), but `createNumber` mistakes the `'.'` for an unrecognized type-qualifier suffix, since `Character.isDigit('.')` is `false`, and falls into the `default:` branch of the suffix `switch`, throwing instead of parsing it as a float/double.

2. **`testIsNumberDecimalWithLongSuffixIsNotActuallyANumber`** — `NumberUtils.isNumber("1.1L")` returns `true`, but `"1.1L"` is not actually parseable as any number: `NumberUtils.createNumber("1.1L")` throws `NumberFormatException` (confirmed by the passing `testCreateNumberDecimalWithLongSuffixThrows`), since a decimal value cannot carry a long (`'L'`) suffix. `isNumber`'s final branch (`chars[i] == 'l' || chars[i] == 'L'`) only checks `foundDigit && !hasExp`, ignoring `hasDecPoint`, so it wrongly validates decimals with an `L` suffix — contradicting its own documented contract ("checks whether the String is a correctly formatted number") and disagreeing with `createNumber` on the same input.
